record.paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Model theory by alteration: (R4)-analogue and model theory after finite extensions
record.original_question: Local uniformization is a local version of resolution of singularities: given a valuation v on the function field F of an algebraic variety, local uniformization asks for a model of F in which the center of v is regular (a non-singular point). It is known (de Jong 1996) that resolution by alteration holds: one can resolve singularities after passing to a finite extension of the function field. Knaf and Kuhlmann (2009) proved local uniformization by alteration for arbitrary valuations: every place on a function field admits local uniformization in a finite extension of that function field. Hypothesis (R4) states that any large field K is existentially closed in any function field F|K that admits a K-rational place. (1) Does local uniformization by alteration imply a reasonable and useful weakening '(R4) by alteration' (perhaps: given a large field K and a function field F|K with a K-rational place, there is a finite extension K'|K such that K' is existentially closed in F.K')? (2) Is there a coherent 'model theory by alteration', i.e., a systematic framework in which model-theoretic properties of valued fields can be established after passing to a finite field extension?

evidence.quote: Open problem 15: Does local uniformization by alteration imply a reasonable (and useful) hypothesis "(R4) by alteration"? Is there a "model theory by alteration"?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Let K be a field. A field K is called large (in the sense of Pop) if every smooth K-curve with a K-rational point has infinitely many K-rational points; equivalently, K is existentially closed in the Laurent series field K((t)).

A function field F | K is a finitely generated field extension F/K. A place of F | K is an equivalence class of valuations on F that are trivial on K; a place P of F | K is called K-rational if its residue field equals K.

Given a valuation v on the function field F of an algebraic variety, local uniformization at v asks for a projective model X of F over the constant field on which the center of v is a regular (non-singular) point. Local uniformization by alteration is the statement (proved by Knaf and Kuhlmann for arbitrary valuations on function fields over a field of any characteristic) that for every place P of F | K, there exists a finite extension F' | F such that the place P admits an extension to F' which has local uniformization on some projective model of F' over the corresponding constant field.

Hypothesis (R4) is the assertion: for every large field K and every function field F | K admitting a K-rational place, the field K is existentially closed in F (i.e. every existential first-order sentence with parameters in K that holds in F also holds in K).

Problems.

(1) Formulate and investigate a "by alteration" weakening of (R4). Specifically, decide whether local uniformization by alteration implies the following statement, or some other natural and useful variant of it:

(R4-alt) For every large field K and every function field F | K admitting a K-rational place, there exists a finite field extension K' | K such that K' is existentially closed in the compositum F·K'.

Determine whether (R4-alt) (or a suitable variant) holds, and identify model-theoretic consequences for valued function fields that follow from it.

(2) Develop a coherent framework of "model theory by alteration": a systematic theory in which model-theoretic properties (such as Ax–Kochen/Ershov-type transfer, existential closedness, completeness or decidability of theories of valued fields) of a valued field, or of a valued function field, are established after passing to a suitable finite field extension. Identify the right axioms for such a framework and prove non-trivial structural results within it.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is explicitly posed as an open question in a 2025 survey on the model theory of tame valued fields. No published resolution of either part — formulating/proving an "(R4) by alteration" or developing a systematic "model theory by alteration" — appears in the literature. Knaf–Kuhlmann (2009) established local uniformization by alteration, and de Jong (1996) established resolution by alteration, but the model-theoretic counterpart is not known to have been developed.
